stem.en: A strong wind blows across dry ground that has dust, sand and gravel on it. What happens to each?

text.en: Gravel rises highest, sand hops low, and dust stays down.

feedback.en: This is the wrong way round. Light grains go furthest, so dust rises and gravel stays.

text.en: Dust, sand and gravel all rise to about the same height.

feedback.en: Size decides how far each goes. Gravel is far too heavy to rise with the dust.

text.en: Dust rises high, sand hops low, and gravel stays down.

feedback.en: Yes. The lighter the grain, the higher and further the wind takes it.

text.en: Sand rises highest, gravel hops low, and dust stays down.

feedback.en: Sand is heavier than dust, so it hops near the ground while dust rises above it.

explanation.en: Wind moves only what it can lift, so size matters. Dust is so light that it rises high and travels far. Sand is heavier and hops along, mostly within a metre of the ground. Gravel is too heavy to lift and stays behind.

hints.en: Think about which of the three is the lightest.
